# Sloc Cloc and Code (scc)

![SCC illustration](./scc.jpg)

A tool similar to cloc, sloccount and tokei. For counting the lines of code, blank lines, comment lines, and physical lines of source code in many programming languages.

Goal is to be the fastest code counter possible, but also perform COCOMO calculation like sloccount, LOCOMO estimation for LLM-based development costs, estimate code complexity similar to cyclomatic complexity calculators and produce unique lines of code or DRYness metrics. In short one tool to rule them all.

Also it has a very short name which is easy to type `scc`.

If you don't like sloc cloc and code feel free to use the name `Succinct Code Counter`.

Licensed under MIT licence.

## Install

### Snap

A snap install exists.

`$ sudo snap install scc`

*NB* Snap installed applications cannot run outside of `/home` so you may encounter issues if you use snap and attempt to run outside this directory.

### Homebrew

Or if you have Homebrew installed

`$ brew install scc`

### Fedora

Fedora Linux users can use a COPR repository:

`$ sudo dnf copr enable lihaohong/scc && sudo dnf install scc`

### MacPorts

On macOS, you can also install via MacPorts

`$ sudo port install scc`

### Scoop

Or if you are using Scoop on Windows

`$ scoop install scc`

### Chocolatey

Or if you are using Chocolatey on Windows

`$ choco install scc`

### WinGet

Or if you are using WinGet on Windows

`winget install --id benboyter.scc --source winget`

### FreeBSD

On FreeBSD, scc is available as a package

`$ pkg install scc`

Or, if you prefer to build from source, you can use the ports tree

`$ cd /usr/ports/devel/scc && make install clean`

### Run in Docker

Go to the directory you want to run scc from.

Run the command below to run the latest release of scc on your current working directory:

```bash
docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD:/pwd"  ghcr.io/boyter/scc:master scc /pwd
```

### Manual

Binaries for Windows, GNU/Linux and macOS for both i386 and x86_64 machines are available from the releases page.

## Usage

Command line usage of `scc` is designed to be as simple as possible.
Full details can be found in `scc --help` or `scc -h`.

```text
Sloc, Cloc and Code. Count lines of code in a directory with complexity estimation.

Usage:
  scc [flags] [files or directories]

Flags:
      --avg-wage int                       average wage value used for basic COCOMO calculation (default 56286)
      --binary                             disable binary file detection
      --by-file                            display output for every file
  -m, --character                          calculate max and mean characters per line
      --ci                                 enable CI output settings where stdout is ASCII
      --cocomo-project-type string         change COCOMO model type [organic, semi-detached, embedded, "custom,1,1,1,1"] (default "organic")
      --count-as string                    count extension as language [e.g. jsp:htm,chead:"C Header" maps extension jsp to html and chead to C Header]
      --count-ignore                       set to allow .gitignore and .ignore files to be counted
      --currency-symbol string             set currency symbol (default "$")
      --debug                              enable debug output
      --directory-walker-job-workers int   controls the maximum number of workers which will walk the directory tree (default 8)
  -a, --dryness                            calculate the DRYness of the project (implies --uloc)
      --eaf float                          the effort adjustment factor derived from the cost drivers (1.0 if rated nominal) (default 1)
      --exclude-dir strings                directories to exclude (default [.git,.hg,.svn])
  -x, --exclude-ext strings                ignore file extensions (overrides include-ext) [comma separated list: e.g. go,java,js]
  -n, --exclude-file strings               ignore files with matching names (default [package-lock.json,Cargo.lock,yarn.lock,pubspec.lock,Podfile.lock,pnpm-lock.yaml])
      --file-gc-count int                  number of files to parse before turning the GC on (default 10000)
      --file-list-queue-size int           the size of the queue of files found and ready to be read into memory (default 8)
      --file-process-job-workers int       number of goroutine workers that process files collecting stats (default 8)
      --file-summary-job-queue-size int    the size of the queue used to hold processed file statistics before formatting (default 8)
  -f, --format string                      set output format [tabular, wide
</output_head>
```

## Unique Lines of Code (ULOC)

ULOC can be used to determine how many DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) code you have. It provides a measurement of unique lines of code.

To get ULOC output use the `--uloc` flag or `-u`:

```text
$ scc --uloc .
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity    ULOC
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076   4,456
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

To calculate DRYness percentage use the `--dryness` flag or `-a`:

```text
$ scc --dryness .
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity    DRYness
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076       74.4%
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

## COCOMO

COCOMO (Constructive Cost Model) calculates the estimated cost to build the code. scc uses the basic COCOMO model to provide estimates.

The COCOMO calculation is always run and will appear at the bottom of the output unless you use `--no-cocomo`.

Example:

```text
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Estimated Cost to Develop (organic) $12,517,562
Estimated Schedule Effort (organic) 35.93 months
Estimated People Required (organic) 30.95
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

You can customize COCOMO calculation with:

- `--avg-wage` - Set the average wage (default 56286)
- `--cocomo-project-type` - Change COCOMO model type: organic, semi-detached, embedded (default "organic")
- `--eaf` - Effort adjustment factor (default 1.0)
- `--currency-symbol` - Set currency symbol (default "$")

## LOCOMO

LOCOMO is an extension of COCOMO for calculating costs when using LLM (Large Language Model) based development approaches. It estimates token counts, API costs, and developer time when using AI assistants.

This is an experimental feature for estimating costs when using AI-powered development tools.

## Output Formats

scc supports multiple output formats for integration with other tools:

- `tabular` (default) - Human-readable table format
- `wide` - Wider table with additional statistics
- `json` - JSON format for programmatic processing
- `json2` - Alternative JSON format
- `csv` - CSV format
- `csv-stream` - Streaming CSV format
- `cloc-yaml` - YAML format compatible with cloc
- `html` - HTML report
- `html-table` - HTML table only
- `sql` - SQL CREATE and INSERT statements
- `sql-insert` - SQL INSERT statements only
- `openmetrics` - OpenMetrics/Prometheus format

Example:

```bash
scc --format json .
scc --format csv --output report.csv .
```

## Ignore Files

`scc` supports .ignore files inside directories that it scans. This is similar to how ripgrep, ag and tokei work. .ignore files are 100% the same as .gitignore files with the same syntax, and as such `scc` will ignore files and directories listed in them. You can add .ignore files to ignore things like vendored dependency checked in files.

By default scc will also respect .gitignore files.

## Large File Detection

scc can identify and optionally exclude large files from counting to focus on code that matters.

Use `--large-line-count` and `--large-byte-count` to set thresholds, and `--no-large` to exclude them from output.

## Minified/Generated File Detection

scc can identify minified and generated files and optionally exclude them from counts.

- `--min` - Identify minified files
- `--gen` - Identify generated files
- `--no-min` - Exclude minified files from output
- `--no-gen` - Exclude generated files from output
- `--no-min-gen` - Exclude both minified and generated files

## Remapping

You can remap file extensions to different languages using the `--count-as` flag:

```bash
scc --count-as jsp:htm,chead:"C Header" .
```

This maps `.jsp` files to HTML and `.chead` files to C Header.

You can also remap based on file content:

- `--remap-unknown` - Check unknown file types for a string and remap
- `--remap-all` - Check all files for a string and remap

Example:

```bash
scc --remap-unknown "-*- C++ -*-":"C Header" .
```

## Badges

You can generate badges for your repository showing lines of code counts.

The service at `https://sloc.xyz/` provides badges for GitHub repositories.

Example badge URL:
```
https://sloc.xyz/github/boyter/scc/
```

# Sloc Cloc and Code (scc)

![SCC illustration](./scc.jpg)

A tool similar to cloc, sloccount and tokei. For counting the lines of code, blank lines, comment lines, and physical lines of source code in many programming languages.

Goal is to be the fastest code counter possible, but also perform COCOMO calculation like sloccount, LOCOMO estimation for LLM-based development costs, estimate code complexity similar to cyclomatic complexity calculators and produce unique lines of code or DRYness metrics. In short one tool to rule them all.

Also it has a very short name which is easy to type `scc`.

If you don't like sloc cloc and code feel free to use the name `Succinct Code Counter`.

Licensed under MIT licence.

## Install

### Snap

A snap install exists.

`$ sudo snap install scc`

*NB* Snap installed applications cannot run outside of `/home` so you may encounter issues if you use snap and attempt to run outside this directory.

### Homebrew

Or if you have Homebrew installed

`$ brew install scc`

### Fedora

Fedora Linux users can use a COPR repository:

`$ sudo dnf copr enable lihaohong/scc && sudo dnf install scc`

### MacPorts

On macOS, you can also install via MacPorts

`$ sudo port install scc`

### Scoop

Or if you are using Scoop on Windows

`$ scoop install scc`

### Chocolatey

Or if you are using Chocolatey on Windows

`$ choco install scc`

### WinGet

Or if you are using WinGet on Windows

`winget install --id benboyter.scc --source winget`

### FreeBSD

On FreeBSD, scc is available as a package

`$ pkg install scc`

Or, if you prefer to build from source, you can use the ports tree

`$ cd /usr/ports/devel/scc && make install clean`

### Run in Docker

Go to the directory you want to run scc from.

Run the command below to run the latest release of scc on your current working directory:

```bash
docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD:/pwd"  ghcr.io/boyter/scc:master scc /pwd
```

### Manual

Binaries for Windows, GNU/Linux and macOS for both i386 and x86_64 machines are available from the releases page.

## Unique Lines of Code (ULOC)

ULOC can be used to determine how many DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) code you have. It provides a measurement of unique lines of code.

To get ULOC output use the `--uloc` flag or `-u`:

```text
$ scc --uloc .
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity    ULOC
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076   4,456
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

To calculate DRYness percentage use the `--dryness` flag or `-a`:

```text
$ scc --dryness .
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity    DRYness
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076       74.4%
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

## COCOMO

COCOMO (Constructive Cost Model) calculates the estimated cost to build the code. scc uses the basic COCOMO model to provide estimates.

The COCOMO calculation is always run and will appear at the bottom of the output unless you use `--no-cocomo`.

Example:

```text
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Estimated Cost to Develop (organic) $12,517,562
Estimated Schedule Effort (organic) 35.93 months
Estimated People Required (organic) 30.95
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

You can customize COCOMO calculation with:

- `--avg-wage` - Set the average wage (default 56286)
- `--cocomo-project-type` - Change COCOMO model type: organic, semi-detached, embedded (default "organic")
- `--eaf` - Effort adjustment factor (default 1.0)
- `--currency-symbol` - Set currency symbol (default "$")

## LOCOMO

LOCOMO is an extension of COCOMO for calculating costs when using LLM (Large Language Model) based development approaches. It estimates token counts, API costs, and developer time when using AI assistants.

This is an experimental feature for estimating costs when using AI-powered development tools.

## Output Formats

scc supports multiple output formats for integration with other tools:

- `tabular` (default) - Human-readable table format
- `wide` - Wider table with additional statistics
- `json` - JSON format for programmatic processing
- `json2` - Alternative JSON format
- `csv` - CSV format
- `csv-stream` - Streaming CSV format
- `cloc-yaml` - YAML format compatible with cloc
- `html` - HTML report
- `html-table` - HTML table only
- `sql` - SQL CREATE and INSERT statements
- `sql-insert` - SQL INSERT statements only
- `openmetrics` - OpenMetrics/Prometheus format

Example:

```bash
scc --format json .
scc --format csv --output report.csv .
```

## Ignore Files

`scc` supports .ignore files inside directories that it scans. This is similar to how ripgrep, ag and tokei work. .ignore files are 100% the same as .gitignore files with the same syntax, and as such `scc` will ignore files and directories listed in them. You can add .ignore files to ignore things like vendored dependency checked in files.

By default scc will also respect .gitignore files.

## Large File Detection

scc can identify and optionally exclude large files from counting to focus on code that matters.

Use `--large-line-count` and `--large-byte-count` to set thresholds, and `--no-large` to exclude them from output.

## Minified/Generated File Detection

scc can identify minified and generated files and optionally exclude them from counts.

- `--min` - Identify minified files
- `--gen` - Identify generated files
- `--no-min` - Exclude minified files from output
- `--no-gen` - Exclude generated files from output
- `--no-min-gen` - Exclude both minified and generated files

## Remapping

You can remap file extensions to different languages using the `--count-as` flag:

```bash
scc --count-as jsp:htm,chead:"C Header" .
```

This maps `.jsp` files to HTML and `.chead` files to C Header.

You can also remap based on file content:

- `--remap-unknown` - Check unknown file types for a string and remap
- `--remap-all` - Check all files for a string and remap

Example:

```bash
scc --remap-unknown "-*- C++ -*-":"C Header" .
```

## Badges

You can generate badges for your repository showing lines of code counts.

The service at `https://sloc.xyz/` provides badges for GitHub repositories.

Example badge URL:
```
https://sloc.xyz/github/boyter/scc/
```

def locomo(path, preset="medium", extra=[]):
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable","--locomo","--locomo-preset",preset,"-f","json2"]+extra+[path],capture_output=True,text=True)
    return json.loads(r.stdout)
def solve(a,b,c,d,e,f): # a x + b y=e ; c x + d y=f
    det=a*d-b*c
    return ((e*d-b*f)/det, (a*f-e*c)/det)
for preset in ["medium","large","small","local"]:
    d1=locomo("/tmp/big",preset); d2=locomo("/tmp/test1",preset)

def batch(ext, contents):

import subprocess,json,os,shutil
EXE=os.path.abspath("./executable")
langs=[line[:line.rfind("(")].strip() for line in open("/tmp/langs.txt")]
bases=[
"if","else","elif","elsif","elseif","for","foreach","forEach","while","do","switch","case","when","catch","try","except","finally",
"and","or","not","match","loop","until","unless","repeat","select","go","defer","func","function","return","break","continue","goto",
"&&","||","??","?","=>","->","#","then","begin","rescue","ensure","raise","throw","throws","in","of","where","with","assert","lambda",
"IF","ELSE","ELSEIF","FOR","FOREACH","WHILE","DO","SWITCH","CASE","WHEN","CATCH","TRY","AND","OR","NOT","MATCH","LOOP","UNTIL","SELECT","THEN","BEGIN",
"If","Else","ElseIf","For","While","Do","Switch","Select","Case","Catch","Try","And","Or","Loop","Until","Then",
"elsIf","ENDIF","END-IF","PERFORM","EVALUATE","WHEN","IF","for_each","forall","where","forall","do concurrent",
"check","on","error","rescue","handle","guard","let","var","sub","proc","each","times","map","filter","reduce","any","all","exists",
"elif","when","unless","until","while","until","for","foreach","loop","match","switch","case","default","catch","except","try",
"fi","done","esac","then","do","done","elif","else","if","for","while","until","case","select"
]
bases=list(dict.fromkeys(bases))
suffixes=[" ","(","{",":",";","["," "]
# tokens as base+suffix, dedup, plus specific symbols compositions
tokens=[]
for b in bases:
    suffs=[" ","(","{",":"] if b not in ["&&","||","??","?","=>","->","#"] else [" ","",":","("]
    for s in suffs: tokens.append(b+s)
tokens += ["else if ","else if(","else {","for each ","for each(","For Each ","Select Case ","end if","endif","fi\n"]
tokens=list(dict.fromkeys([t for t in tokens if "\n" not in t]))
print("tokens",len(tokens))

def run_language(lang):
    d="/tmp/lang_probe_dir"; shutil.rmtree(d,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(d)
    for i,tok in enumerate(tokens):
        content=f"{tok}x\n"
        open(os.path.join(d,f"f{i:04}.sccprobe"),"wb").write(content.encode())
    r=subprocess.run([EXE,"--count-as",f"sccprobe:{lang}","-f","json","--by-file",d],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=30)
    j=json.loads(r.stdout) if r.stdout.strip() else []
    by={}
    for s in j:
        for f in s["Files"]: by[f["Filename"]]=f["Complexity"]
    hits=[tok for i,tok in enumerate(tokens) if by.get(f"f{i:04}.sccprobe",0)>0]
    # Also counts >1 note
    counts={tok:by.get(f"f{i:04}.sccprobe") for i,tok in enumerate(tokens) if by.get(f"f{i:04}.sccprobe",0)}
    return {"hits":hits,"counts":counts}
out={}
for i,lang in enumerate(langs):
    try: out[lang]=run_language(lang)
    except Exception as e: out[lang]={"error":str(e),"hits":[]}
    if i%50==0: print(i,lang,out[lang].get("hits"),flush=True)
json.dump({"tokens":tokens,"results":out},open("/tmp/lang_complexity.json","w"),indent=1)
print("done")

FLAG_BY_NAME = {d[0]: d for d in FLAG_DEFS}
FLAG_BY_SHORT = {d[1]: d for d in FLAG_DEFS if d[1]}

class FlagError(Exception):
    pass

class Options:
    pass

def flag_display_name(defn):
    name, short = defn[0], defn[1]
    if short:
        return f'"-{short}, --{name}"'
    return f'"--{name}"'

def set_flag_value(opts, changed, defn, raw_value_str):
    name, short, typ, default, usage = defn
    key = name.replace("-", "_")
    try:
        if typ == "bool":
            val = parse_go_bool(raw_value_str)
        elif typ == "int":
            val = parse_go_int(raw_value_str)
        elif typ == "float":
            val = parse_go_float(raw_value_str)
        elif typ == "string":
            val = raw_value_str
        elif typ == "strings":
            try:
                vals = parse_csv_record(raw_value_str)
            except CsvParseError as e:
                raise FlagError(f'invalid argument "{raw_value_str}" for {flag_display_name(defn)} flag: {e}')
            if name not in changed:
                setattr(opts, key, list(vals))
            else:
                getattr(opts, key).extend(vals)
            changed.add(name)
            return
        elif typ == "stringArray":
            if name not in changed:
                # default empty; pflag stringArray first set does not clear non-empty default in newer versions? default here empty.
                setattr(opts, key, [raw_value_str])
            else:
                getattr(opts, key).append(raw_value_str)
            changed.add(name)
            return
        else:
            val = raw_value_str
    except GoParseError as e:
        raise FlagError(f'invalid argument "{raw_value_str}" for {flag_display_name(defn)} flag: {e.msg}')
    setattr(opts, key, val)
    changed.add(name)

def default_options():
    o = Options()
    for name, short, typ, default, usage in FLAG_DEFS:
        key = name.replace("-", "_")
        if isinstance(default, list):
            setattr(o, key, list(default))
        else:
            setattr(o, key, default)
    o._changed = set()
    # output default in help says stdout but actual default value used in code is "" (empty). Keep "".
    return o

def parse_flags(args, allow_completion_flags=False):
    """Parse root flags interspersed with positionals. Returns (opts, positionals).
    Raises FlagError with message (without 'Error:' prefix)."""
    opts = default_options()
    changed = opts._changed
    positionals = []
    i = 0
    end_flags = False
    while i < len(args):
        arg = args[i]
        if end_flags:
            positionals.append(arg); i += 1; continue
        if arg == "--":
            end_flags = True; i += 1; continue
        if len(arg) >= 2 and arg[0] == "-" and arg[1] == "-":
            # long
            body = arg[2:]
            if body == "":
                positionals.append(arg); i += 1; continue
            if "=" in body:
                name, value = body.split("=", 1)
                has_value = True
            else:
                name, value, has_value = body, None, False
            defn = FLAG_BY_NAME.get(name)
            if defn is None and allow_completion_flags and name == "no-descriptions":
                # handled outside
                defn = ("no-descriptions", "", "bool", False, "disable completion descriptions")
                if not hasattr(opts, "no_descriptions"):
                    opts.no_descriptions = False
            if defn is None:
                raise FlagError(f"unknown flag: --{name}")
            typ = defn[2]
            if typ == "bool":
                if has_value:
                    set_flag_value(opts, changed, defn, value)
                else:
                    # set true directly
                    setattr(opts, defn[0].replace("-", "_"), True)
                    changed.add(defn[0])
                i += 1; continue
            else:
                if not has_value:
                    if i + 1 >= len(args):
                        raise FlagError(f"flag needs an argument: --{name}")
                    value = args[i+1]; i += 2
                else:
                    i += 1
                set_flag_value(opts, changed, defn, value)
                continue
        elif len(arg) >= 2 and arg[0] == "-" and arg != "-":
            # shorthand cluster
            cluster = arg[1:]
            pos = 0
            consumed_next = False
            while pos < len(cluster):
                ch = cluster[pos]
                defn = FLAG_BY_SHORT.get(ch)
                if defn is None:
                    remaining = cluster[pos:]
                    raise FlagError(f"unknown shorthand flag: '{ch}' in -{remaining}")
                typ = defn[2]
                rest = cluster[pos+1:]
                if typ == "bool":
                    if rest.startswith("="):
                        set_flag_value(opts, changed, defn, rest[1:])
                        pos = len(cluster); break
                    else:
                        setattr(opts, defn[0].replace("-", "_"), True)
                        changed.add(defn[0])
                        pos += 1; continue
                else:
                    if rest != "":
                        value = rest[1:] if rest.startswith("=") else rest
                        set_flag_value(opts, changed, defn, value)
                        pos = len(cluster); break
                    else:
                        if i + 1 >= len(args):
                            raise FlagError(f"flag needs an argument: '{ch}' in -{ch}")
                        value = args[i+1]; consumed_next = True
                        set_flag_value(opts, changed, defn, value)
                        pos = len(cluster); break
            i += 2 if consumed_next else 1
            continue
        else:
            positionals.append(arg); i += 1; continue
    return opts, positionals

def print_flag_error(msg, usage_text):
    sys.stderr.write(f"Error: {msg}\n")
    sys.stderr.write(usage_text)
    sys.stderr.write("\n")

import subprocess, sys, os, difflib
REF="/workspace/executable"; NEW="/tmp/my_scc"
def run(exe,args,cwd=None,env=None):
    return subprocess.run([exe]+args,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=10,cwd=cwd)
def compare(args,cwd=None,label=None):
    r1=run(REF,args,cwd); r2=run(NEW,args,cwd)
    ok=(r1.returncode==r2.returncode and r1.stdout==r2.stdout and r1.stderr==r2.stderr)
    print(("OK " if ok else "DIFF ")+(label or " ".join(args)))
    if not ok:

            print(" STDERR DIFF---ref +++new")

                print(l)
    return ok

package math

func isOddInt(x float64) bool {
	if Abs(x) >= (1 << 53) {
		// 1 << 53 is the largest exact integer in the float64 format.
		// Any number outside this range will be truncated before the decimal point and therefore will always be
		// an even integer.
		// Without this check and if x overflows int64 the int64(xi) conversion below may produce incorrect results

		return false

	xi, xf := Modf(x)
	return xf == 0 && int64(xi)&1 == 1

	}
